methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes source structure (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/OR.json), corrected against raw OCR of the chapter's own two-column TOC (pdf 1089) and ~25 body pages. OR presented the most severe source-structure corruption found to date: the printed Toronto Notes TOC for this chapter is a genuine two-column layout (left column: Acronyms through Hip; right column: Femur through References), and the automated extraction pipeline read it as a single interleaved stream, merging left-column row N with right-column row N into a single garbled toc_inventory.json node/title for most of the chapter (e.g. OR.S10 'Rotator Cuff Disease Ankle' = left 'Rotator Cuff Disease' + right 'Ankle'). Beyond simple title merges, this produced two further defect classes: (1) MISSING SECTIONS -- entire right-column sections with no left-column counterpart row available to merge into (Fractures General Principles, Articular Cartilage, Orthopedic X-Ray Imaging, the Orthopedic Emergencies section header itself, the Shoulder section header itself, Femur, most of Knee, most of Foot, Achilles tendon pathology, Plantar Fasciitis, Bunions) are entirely absent from toc_inventory.json -- confirmed via the 5-entry research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json UNRESOLVED list plus direct body-OCR confirmation for headings unresolved went further than the ledger even flagged; (2) WRONG PARENT -- OR.S16.T01-T03 ('Fractures of the Spine', 'Cervical Spine', 'Thoracolumbar Spine') are parented under OR.S16 'References' in toc_inventory.json, but body OCR confirms they are children of the real 'Spine' section (co-located with 'Hand' on the same TOC row, per OR.S04's merged_duplicate_headings), not References sub-topics -- the row-based merge attached them to whichever S0X node the interleaved stream had reached by that point. All corrections below are resolved via raw OCR body-page confirmation (never model memory/medical-knowledge reconstruction) and cited per-unit; sections/topics with no surviving toc_inventory.json node are sourced from synthetic UNCATALOGUED:<Name>@pdf<N> ids per the chapter-A 'Monitoring' / OP.S19 'UvealTract' precedent. No page-image rendering was performed for this pass -- resolution relied on raw body-text OCR, which was sufficient and internally consistent at every point checked (~25 spot verifications across the chapter); flagged in review_items.json for optional human page-image confirmation given the scale of reconstruction. Excluded as non-clinical organizational/reference material: the chapter root (OR), the Acronyms portion of OR.S01 (matches the OP.S01/OB.S01/NS.S01 chapter-opening acronym-glossary precedent), OR.S15 (Landmark Orthopedic Trials -- an EBM-summary table, consistent with the OP.S20/OB.S18/NS.S20 References-section precedent), and OR.S16 (References -- its three substantive T-children are retained, correctly re-parented under Spine, as SU-OR-33 through SU-OR-35).

study_units.title: Approach to Fractures, Fracture Healing, and General Fracture Complications
study_units.structural_rationale: research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json records 'Basic Anatomy Review'/'Articular Cartilage'/'Orthopedic X-RayImaging'/'Orthopedic Emergencies' as UNRESOLVED (page-anchor could not be confirmed by the automated pipeline) and toc_inventory.json contains no node at all for this section ('Fractures eneral Principles' in the raw TOC OCR, i.e. 'Fractures General Principles') or its three sub-topics (Approach to Fractures, Fracture Healing, General Fracture Complications) -- confirmed missing from the full 55-node packet dump. Independently resolved via raw OCR of pdf 1089 (chapter TOC, two-column layout) and body pages 1093-1094 (OR5-OR6), which confirm this is a real generic-principles section (fracture description/classification terminology, healing stages, and the general complication list -- malunion/nonunion/AVN/infection/compartment syndrome -- that individual fracture units below cross-reference as 'see General Fracture Complications, OR7'). Represented as a single grouped unit per the project instruction not to fragment generic principles content; sourced from a synthetic UNCATALOGUED id since no toc_inventory.json node exists to cite.
